question: What share of the bio-oil model's total sum of squares does temperature account for?
rendered:
From the document, in the section "Table 2: Analysis of variance (ANOVA) for product yields (Bio-char, Bio-oil, and Bio-gas) from teak tree leaves", under "Response 2: Bio Oil (%)", we can see the following information:

| Source        | Sum of Squares | Df | Mean Square | F-value | p-value |
|---------------|----------------|----|-------------|---------|---------|
| Model         | 337.71         | 8  | 42.19       | 120.73  | < 0.0001|
| A-Temperature  | 223.60         | 4  | 55.90       | 148.17  | < 0.0001|
| B-Time        | 114.11         | 4  | 28.53       | 75.62   | < 0.0001|
| Residual      | 6.04           | 16 | 0.378       |         |         |
| Cor Total     | 343.74         | 24 |             |         |         |

The sum of squares for the model is 337.71. The sum of squares for temperature (A-Temperature) is 223.60.

To find the share of the bio-oil model's total sum of squares that temperature accounts for, we can divide the sum of squares for temperature by the total sum of squares for the model:

(223.60 / 337.71) * 100% ≈ 66.1%

So, temperature accounts for approximately 66.1% of the bio-oil model's total sum of squares.
